memory_candidates.content: When a plan's docstring-recording phase must name declarations that a LATER, independent phase of the same plan will land (e.g. 'name the library halves landed in Phases 1 and 3' written into a phase-2 task when phase 3 has not yet run), the forward reference is safe to write verbatim as long as the current phase's own verification scope (a single-module build) has no import dependency on the not-yet-landed module. The docstring becomes fully accurate once the later phase lands; nothing in the current phase's own build surface can observe the gap in the interim. Do not narrow the plan's instructed wording to avoid the forward reference -- that would be scope renegotiation, not execution.

A plan's own prior-phase precedent ('row descriptions are preserved across --emit-inventory regeneration, so this is a hand edit of the description cell only -- never of a generated count cell') generalizes across every later phase touching the same generated README inventory table, not just the phase that first stated it. When editing a module's inventory-row description after a line-count-changing edit, update only the description cell and leave the line-count cell at its pre-edit value; the count is corrected later by the plan's own --emit-inventory regeneration phase.
